title: Offer a specific apology and proportionate repair

sections.title: Understand the distinction
sections.body: An apology owns the particular action and known effect without claiming all possible harm or demanding absolution. A repair offer must be feasible, welcome and proportionate.

sections.title: Complete fictional practice material
sections.body: Ari borrowed Jo’s ruler, due Tuesday 17:00 at the staffed desk. Ari forgot and returns Wednesday 09:00. Jo spent 10 minutes finding an alternative Tuesday but bought nothing. Jo permits one written message and asks for the ruler at the desk; no visit or gift is requested. The desk confirms Wednesday receipt.

sections.title: Work through the supplied case
sections.body: Write the apology and prevention step using action, intention, negligence and impact separately. Identify what is already repaired and what remains unknown.

sections.title: Try a different case before checking
sections.body: A repair offer is declined because the affected person has another arrangement. Is doing it anyway necessary to prove remorse?

checks.title: Compare reasoning and review the supplied result
checks.body: Own the late return and 10-minute burden; accidental forgetting does not erase responsibility. Acknowledge desk receipt and a reminder for future loans without demanding trust. Later fiction: Jo acknowledges the message but declines another loan. Partial: express regret without naming the missed deadline. Incorrect: invent financial loss, insist on a visit or count acknowledgment as forgiveness.
criteria: Action and known impact are specific
Repair fits the recipient’s stated limits
Forgiveness and future trust are not presumed

checks.title: Check the changed case
checks.body: No. Respect the refusal and use a legitimate prevention/accountability route. The affected person need not host a repair performance or supply reassurance.
